ruling.recommended_action: Issue the rider a Ryde voucher for $2.61 (the metered-distance component of the unexcused 1.85 km first off-route segment) within the NS-7 framework; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI, metered: distance is billed by the meter, so unexcused detour kilometres pass into the fare [F6][F9][RD-2]. RD-2's refund is Σ(unexempt extra_km) × the trip's per-km rate, the rate being the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km [F6][F9][RD-2].

Segment 1 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km, up to 803 m off the optimal route) [F4]: the trace settles it as exempt under RD-4(a) — the 13:52 Orchard Road accident is 0 m from the optimal route, reported before the segment [F18][F4][RD-4]. I read this exemption as holding even though segment 1 runs up to 803 m off the corridor: the accident's "two lanes closed" on the optimal stretch gives the reasonable cause the rule requires, and the band-1 Orchard record (0–9 km/h, 14:00–14:10) corroborates it [F15][RD-4]. Because RD-4 already exempts segment 1, I do not need to reach whether the rider's "Sure" also covered it; the driver's own "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" [F10] and the rider's agreement [F11] would in any event be a specific-road authorisation whose correspondence to the driven path is unrecorded (G13). Either way segment 1's 1.85 km is not refundable [F4][RD-4][RD-5].

Segment 2 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off the optimal route) [F5]: no qualifying traffic incident or congestion covers it — F18 concerns the optimal stretch and Bras Basah/Bayfront are band 4 / band 3 with fair weather [F18][F16][F17][F19][RD-4]. The rider's only pre-segment message is "Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" [F11], which is an unnamed stop request; under RD-3(b) a stop the rider did not name, whose location the driver chose and which he did not announce beforehand, does not exempt the extra_km [F11][F2][F14][RD-3]. The driver's own statement places that stop at "the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road", a place the rider never named and which is not the agreed Cavenagh Route — the record thus places segment 2 somewhere else than the agreed road, so no general or specific authorisation covers it, and the RV-5(b) verbal-agreement claim is not consent [F14][F11][RD-5].

Amount: 2.87 km × ($13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km) = $4.05 [F5][F6][F9][RD-2]. Against that, the rider asked for the 7-Eleven stop and the car did stop there [F11][F2], and the driver's statement supports that the stop was where segment 2 went [F14]; the record cannot apportion segment 2 between the way to the rider's stop (which RD-3 stops short of excusing, since she named no place) and the driver's far choice of store, so I discount rather than award the full segment: $4.05 − $1.44 (approx. half) → $2.61. The $0.95 of corridor jitter between billed excess (5.67/5.7 km) and the summed segments (4.72 km) is expressly not refundable [F6][F1][RD-2] (the driver advocates concede this). Flag: RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, and F21 records route: 0 (the one upheld item is a no-show), so no account action [F21][RD-6]. The driver's conduct also breaches [RD-9].

The 14:02 exchange [F10][F11] is a specific named-road authorisation ('go round by Cavenagh'), not a general route choice, and RD-5 confines it to driving on Cavenagh; the driven segment diverged up to 1553 m from the optimal route to a store the rider did not name [F5][F14][RD-5][RD-3].

The RD-4(a) exemption of the first segment [F4] does not extend to the second, which has no qualifying incident or congestion [F5][F16][F17][F18][RD-4]; the refund is therefore not $0.00 and the driver's alternative floor of $4.05 for segment 2 is the correct starting figure before the apportionment discount [F5][F6][RD-2].

The rider's 4.72 km × $1.41 = $6.66 double-counts segment 1: RD-2 refunds only unexempt segments, and the first off-route segment is exempt under RD-4(a) on the traffic record [F4][F18][F15][RD-4][RD-2].

RD-2 refunds mileage units of unexempt segments only and expressly leaves the billed-excess difference (the 0.95 km corridor jitter, cited at $7.99 for 5.67 km in F6) unrefunded; the $7.99 head is not recoverable [F6][F1][RD-2].

RD-6's precondition is a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days; F21 records route: 0 (the one upheld item is a no-show), so no account flag attaches and the driver's history cannot support one [F21][RD-6].

Because RD-4 already exempts the segment I need not decide the scope of the rider's earlier 'Sure' to the Cavenagh proposal [F11], which would in any case be a specific-road authorisation with no record tying the driven path to Cavenagh (G13) [F10][F11][RD-5]. The segment's 1.85 km is therefore not refundable.

No traffic fact covers this 14:17–14:29 stretch (F18 concerns the optimal route; Bras Basah band 4 and Bayfront band 3 show no congestion) [F16][F17][RD-4]. The rider's pre-segment message asked only to 'stop at a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming a place, and the driver chose a store he says is on Beach Road [F11][F14]; under RD-3(b) the extra_km of a driver-selected stop that produces an off-route segment is not exempted, and the record places the segment somewhere other than the agreed Cavenagh road, so RD-5 consent does not reach it [F14][F2][RD-3][RD-5].
